title: Singapore PDPC fines law firm Rajah & Tann S$247,000 over 2023 data breach
date_note: The Star reports the PDPC published its report on 25 November; the breach itself was in July 2023.
geo_basis: country/city of the regulator and firm as given by the source (Singapore)
summary: The Star reports that Singapore's Personal Data Protection Commission fined Rajah & Tann S$247,000 after an attacker bypassed multi-factor authentication, obtained an administrator account's credentials and stole personal data from a network server. The firm put the number of victims at 143,756 people, which the PDPC said could be lower. The PDPC found the firm lacked protocols for responding to a vendor's alerts, which a cybersecurity manager dismissed in July 2023.
plain: Singapore's data regulator fined law firm Rajah & Tann S$247,000 after a 2023 breach. The Star reports the firm put the number of victims at 143,756 people.
exec: The PDPC found the firm had no protocols for acting on vendor alerts; the fine is S$247,000.
impact: The firm put the number of victims at 143,756 people (the PDPC said it could be lower); the PDPC found no evidence the data was leaked on the dark web or internet, The Star reports.

evidence.quote: Top Singapore law firm Rajah & Tann has been fined S$247,000 for a data breach
the law firm put the number of victims at 143,756 people
the personal data of up to 143,756 people was stolen

validation.note: Two independent publishers, The Star and VnExpress International, each report the S$247,000 PDPC fine and the 143,756 figure (VnExpress: "up to 143,756"); the PDPC decision itself was not read.
